classification.difficultyReason: For each supplied opposite side-angle pair, apply inverse sine, generate the supplementary candidate and test it against the triangle angle sum; checking multiple solutions is explicitly prompted.

content.prompt:
[Ambiguous case of the sine rule]

Find $\theta$ in the following questions, and be careful to check if there is more than one solution. For the cases that do have more than one solution, draw both possible triangles. Give angles to the nearest minute.

spec.description: Schematic triangle with horizontal base 7, right side 5, apex angle 60 degrees and theta at the lower-left vertex. No added vertex labels, ticks, fill or units.
spec.mathematics: The side opposite theta is 5 and the side opposite 60 degrees is 7.

answer.short:
$\theta=38^\circ13'$. One triangle is possible.

The supplementary angle fails the triangle angle-sum check.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{5}&=\frac{\sin60^\circ}{7}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{5\sin60^\circ}{7}\\\theta_1&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{5\sin60^\circ}{7}\right)\\\theta_1&\approx38^\circ13'\\\theta_2&=180^\circ-\theta_1\\\theta_2&\approx141^\circ47'.\end{align*}$$
Since $141^\circ47'+60^\circ>180^\circ$, reject the supplementary angle. Thus $\theta=38^\circ13'$ is the only solution; no second triangle can be drawn.

spec.description: Schematic triangle with horizontal lower side 6, upper vertex to the right of the lower-right vertex, right sloping side 10, lower-left angle 30 degrees and theta at the upper vertex. No added vertex labels, ticks, fill or units.
spec.mathematics: The side opposite theta is 6 and the side opposite 30 degrees is 10.

answer.short:
$\theta=17^\circ27'$. One triangle is possible.

The supplementary angle fails the triangle angle-sum check.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{6}&=\frac{\sin30^\circ}{10}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{6\sin30^\circ}{10}\\\sin\theta&=0.3\\\theta_1&=\sin^{-1}(0.3)\\\theta_1&\approx17^\circ27'\\\theta_2&=180^\circ-\theta_1\\\theta_2&\approx162^\circ33'.\end{align*}$$
Since $162^\circ33'+30^\circ>180^\circ$, reject the supplementary angle. Thus $\theta=17^\circ27'$ is the only solution; no second triangle can be drawn.
